## DynamicWireValue type

A value in dynamic content, where no schema describes the shape.

**Signature:**

```typescript
type DynamicWireValue =
  | string
  | boolean
  | null
  | WireInteger
  | WireDouble
  | WireDate
  | DynamicRecordWire
  | readonly DynamicWireValue[]
```

**References:** [WireInteger](./contracts.wireinteger.md)<!-- -->, [WireDouble](./contracts.wiredouble.md)<!-- -->, [WireDate](./contracts.wiredate.md)<!-- -->, [DynamicRecordWire](./contracts.dynamicrecordwire.md)<!-- -->, [DynamicWireValue](./contracts.dynamicwirevalue.md)

## Remarks

Strings, booleans, and `null` stand for themselves; arrays hold encoded elements; every object is a control record. Numbers of unknown native classification are encoded as doubles.

References, file values, and file sources appear only at typed positions, never in dynamic content. Decoding a reference needs its resource's identifier type, which an `unknown` position does not name, and a file value carries a runtime-issued grant that dynamic content cannot establish. So [WireReference](./contracts.wirereference.md)<!-- -->, [WireFile](./contracts.wirefile.md)<!-- -->, and [WireFileSource](./contracts.wirefilesource.md) are not members of this type.
